title: Gate a VCF Automation day-2 resource action behind an availability precheck
prompt:
Implement `VcfAutomationDay2.psm1`, a PowerShell 7 module that submits a VCF Automation 9.1 day-2 resource action only after a precheck confirms the action is available. Edit no other file and add no dependency.

VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize and Aria Automation, and unlike the rest of VMware Cloud Foundation it publishes no machine-readable API description. It is absent from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, and the VMware.Sdk.Vcf PowerCLI family (SddcManager, CloudBuilder, Installer, Ops) contains no Automation module. Do not vendor an SDK, and do not invent a `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Automation` dependency. Call the REST API directly with PowerShell's built-in web cmdlets.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is the wire contract. It was transcribed by hand from the rendered VCF Automation 9.1 xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com, each of which is recorded in `docs/official_sources.json` together with the operation it documents and the date it was fetched. The contract states plainly that its source is reference documentation rather than a published specification, so its `contract_operation_id` values are local labels only; never put one on the wire. Use exactly the three operations it names, `getDeploymentResources`, `getResourceActions` and `submitResourceActionRequest`, and call no other route.

Preserve the supplied public surface. `Connect-VcfAutomationServer -Server -AccessToken -Port -Protocol` returns a connection object and performs no HTTP; `AccessToken` is a SecureString and the returned object must never expose it in plain text. `Invoke-VcfAutomationResourceAction -Connection -DeploymentId -ResourceName -ActionId [-Reason] [-Inputs]` performs the workflow and returns exactly one report object. Keep both functions exported and no others.

The workflow is three steps and the precheck gates the last one. First call `getDeploymentResources` for the deployment, filtered to the requested resource name, and resolve the resource id by an exact case-sensitive name match. Then call `getResourceActions` for that resource id: this is the precheck. Submit `submitResourceActionRequest` only when the returned array contains an action whose `id` matches `ActionId` exactly and whose `valid` member is true. When the resource is missing, when the action is not offered for that resource, or when the action is offered but not valid, stop before the mutating call so the deployment is left untouched, and return the report rather than throwing.

The report is a single object whose properties appear in this order: `Outcome`, `DeploymentId`, `ResourceName`, `ResourceId`, `ActionId`, `PrecheckStatus`, `PrecheckDetail`, `RequestId`, `RequestStatus`. `Outcome` is `Submitted` or `Blocked`. `PrecheckStatus` is `Passed`, `ResourceNotFound`, `ActionNotAvailable` or `ActionNotValid`. `PrecheckDetail` is null when the precheck passes and a nonblank explanation otherwise. `ResourceId` is null only when the resource could not be resolved. `RequestId` and `RequestStatus` carry the submitted request's `id` and `status` on success and are null whenever the precheck blocks. The report must never expose the access token.

Honor the exact wire contract. Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` and `Accept: application/json`. Both reads are bodyless GETs that omit `Content-Type` and transfer encoding. The `getDeploymentResources` request sends the `names` query parameter set to the requested resource name and nothing else, so `resourceTypes`, `tags`, `expand`, `page`, `size`, `sort`, `$top`, `$skip`, `$orderby` and `$filter` are all absent. The `getResourceActions` and `submitResourceActionRequest` requests send no query string at all. The submission is a POST with exactly one `application/json` content type and a JSON object body. Every member of `ResourceActionRequest` is optional, so send `actionId` always, send `inputs` only when `-Inputs` is supplied and holds at least one entry, send `reason` only when `-Reason` is supplied, and emit the members in the contract's documented order: `actionId`, `inputs`, `reason`. Omission means the member is absent, never null, blank, an empty object or any other placeholder. Preserve input value types, so a boolean input stays a JSON boolean.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier starts the shipped loopback mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port once per scenario and reads its request log and its log of state changes actually applied. The mock builds its route table from `docs/contract.json`, so it serves only the three operations the contract names and records anything else as an off-contract call. Verification asserts the resolved resource, the precheck decision, the report shape and values, the exact request sequence, method, path, path parameters, query parameters, headers and JSON body member order, that every unset optional field is omitted, and that a failed precheck produces no submission and no state change. The verifier contacts no live VMware endpoint.

source_basis.reference_title: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Deployment
source_basis.sdk_module_coverage: none of the four VMware.Sdk.Vcf PowerCLI modules covers VCF Automation

scenario: A day-2 resource action is submitted against a VCF Automation deployment only when the resource resolves and the resource-actions precheck reports the action as offered and valid; a missing resource, an unoffered action and an offered-but-invalid action each stop the workflow before the mutating request.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact wire shape, the omission of every unset optional query and body member, and that a failed precheck submits nothing and changes nothing.
